name: Field Doctor-Style Veggie Bean Chilli (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
535 g Whole grain rice
480 g Red Kidney Beans
1/2 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
2 1/2 medium Carrots
1 1/2 Green Peppers
205 g Smoked Tofu [Water, SOYA Beans, Nigari]
90 g Red Quinoa
2 1/2 tbsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
27 g Chives
1 1/2 tbsp Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt]
6 tbsp Coriander
3 tbsp Pumpkin Seed
1 1/4 tbsp Tapioca Starch
1 3/4 tsp Brown Sugar
1 tbsp Cumin Ground
2 tsp Sweet Noble Paprika
1 1/2 tsp Smoked Paprika
1/2 tsp Sea Salt
1 tsp Chipotle chilli
1/2 tsp Oregano
1/2 tsp Cinnamon Ground
directions:
1. Grains: Rinse and cook wholegrain rice and red quinoa in salted water until tender; drain and keep warm.

2. Chilli base: Soften carrot, green pepper and chives in extra virgin olive oil. Stir in cumin, sweet paprika, smoked paprika, oregano, cinnamon and a pinch of chipotle.

3. Simmer: Add drained red kidney beans, chopped tomato, tomato puree, diced smoked tofu, tamari, brown sugar and enough water to make a stew. Simmer 20–25 minutes until thick; finish with a tapioca slurry if needed.

4. Serve: Spoon chilli over the rice–quinoa mix. Top with coriander and toasted pumpkin seeds.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Ingredients: Water, Whole grain rice, Red Kidney Beans, Chopped Tomato, Carrot, Green Pepper, Smoked Tofu [Water, SOYA Beans, Nigari], Extra Virgin Olive Oil...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Veggie Bean Chilli (Low FODMAP) (~363 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/3-bean-smoked-tofu-chilli-1
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~363 g x 8 = 2904 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~566 g (inferred ~19.50% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~89 g (inferred ~3.06% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
